# Typing special characters (v32io adapter)

*Generated by `tools/gen-charset.py`; the tables are in `firmware/RP2350-USB-A/src/compose_table.h`.*

A USB keyboard only tells the adapter *which key* was pressed, not what the
computer's keyboard layout makes of it, so the adapter has its own way of typing
the characters of the Vircon32 BIOS font that are not on a US keyboard. It is
meant for a US layout, and it works with the **right Alt** key (AltGr; right
Option on a Mac) and with **Alt codes** on the numeric keypad. Everything else
(letters, numbers, shift...) is unchanged, and so is any program that
doesn't read typed characters.

The right Alt and left Alt keys are still reported to the program as keys.
Only the keys *typed together with them*, when they type something here, are
kept from being reported as keys (otherwise `AltGr` `e` would type both `é`
and `e`). A combination that is not listed below works as it always did.

## AltGr + key

Modelled on the US-International layout. A second column shows what the same
key types with Shift held; `-` means shift changes nothing.

| Key | AltGr | AltGr + Shift |

| `2` | ² (0xB2) | - |
| `3` | ³ (0xB3) | - |

## Dead keys

Press the dead key combination, release it, then press a letter: the accent is
put on it (hold Shift for a capital letter, or have Caps Lock on).
The same dead key twice, or a dead key followed by space, types the accent
itself; followed by a letter that can't take it, you get the accent and then
the letter.

| Dead key | Typed with | Letters it combines with |
| -------- | ---------- | ------------------------ |
| acute `´` | AltGr + ' | ÁÉÍÓÚÝáéíóúý |
| grave ``` | AltGr + ` | ÀÈÌÒÙàèìòù |
| circumflex `^` | AltGr + Shift + 6 | ÂÊÎÔÛâêîôû |
| diaeresis `¨` | AltGr + Shift + ' | ÄËÏÖÜŸäëïöüÿ |
| tilde `~` | AltGr + Shift + ` | ÃÕÑãõñ |

## Alt codes

Hold the **left** Alt key, type the character's decimal code on the **numeric
keypad** (up to 4 digits; leading zeros are fine), then release Alt. This works
for every character of the BIOS font, including the box drawing ones, with the
code of the table below (`Alt` `0` `2` `3` `3` types `é`). A code that has no
glyph types nothing.

| Code | Character | Code | Character | Code | Character | Code | Character |
| ---- | --------- | ---- | --------- | ---- | --------- | ---- | --------- |
| 14 | ⬚ | 150 | – | 187 | » | 222 | Þ |
| 15 | ▯ | 151 | — | 188 | ¼ | 223 | ß |
| 17 | ░ | 152 | ˜ | 189 | ½ | 224 | à |
| 18 | ▒ | 153 | ™ | 190 | ¾ | 225 | á |
| 19 | ▓ | 154 | š | 191 | ¿ | 226 | â |
| 20 | █ | 155 | › | 192 | À | 227 | ã |
| 21 | ─ | 156 | œ | 193 | Á | 228 | ä |
| 22 | │ | 158 | ž | 194 | Â | 229 | å |
| 23 | ┘ | 159 | Ÿ | 195 | Ã | 230 | æ |
| 24 | ┐ | 161 | ¡ | 196 | Ä | 231 | ç |
| 25 | ┌ | 162 | ¢ | 197 | Å | 232 | è |
| 26 | └ | 163 | £ | 198 | Æ | 233 | é |
| 27 | ├ | 164 | ¤ | 199 | Ç | 234 | ê |
| 28 | ┤ | 165 | ¥ | 200 | È | 235 | ë |
| 29 | ┴ | 166 | ¦ | 201 | É | 236 | ì |
| 30 | ┬ | 167 | § | 202 | Ê | 237 | í |
| 31 | ┼ | 168 | ¨ | 203 | Ë | 238 | î |
| 128 | € | 169 | © | 204 | Ì | 239 | ï |
| 130 | ‚ | 170 | ª | 205 | Í | 240 | ð |
| 131 | ƒ | 171 | « | 206 | Î | 241 | ñ |
| 132 | „ | 172 | ¬ | 207 | Ï | 242 | ò |
| 133 | … | 173 | ­ | 208 | Ð | 243 | ó |
| 134 | † | 174 | ® | 209 | Ñ | 244 | ô |
| 135 | ‡ | 175 | ¯ | 210 | Ò | 245 | õ |
| 136 | ˆ | 176 | ° | 211 | Ó | 246 | ö |
| 137 | ‰ | 177 | ± | 212 | Ô | 247 | ÷ |
| 138 | Š | 178 | ² | 213 | Õ | 248 | ø |
| 139 | ‹ | 179 | ³ | 214 | Ö | 249 | ù |
| 140 | Œ | 180 | ´ | 215 | × | 250 | ú |
| 142 | Ž | 181 | µ | 216 | Ø | 251 | û |
| 145 | ‘ | 182 | ¶ | 217 | Ù | 252 | ü |
| 146 | ’ | 183 | · | 218 | Ú | 253 | ý |
| 147 | “ | 184 | ¸ | 219 | Û | 254 | þ |
| 148 | ” | 185 | ¹ | 220 | Ü | 255 | ÿ |
| 149 | • | 186 | º | 221 | Ý |  |  |

The codes 32 to 126 (ASCII) also work, and anything else (0 to 13, 16, 127 and
the codes the BIOS font does not use) types nothing.

On the emulator side none of this is needed: the host operating system's own
keyboard layout, dead keys and compose keys type the characters (see
`emulator/README.md`).
